chapters.title: Chapter 882 Holy Righteous Heretics
paragraphs: "Haa we just wanted a backup at first, but your father... I misjudged my capabilities, we ended up getting a triplet." The monk's voice carried a note of resignation, as if he still couldn't quite believe it himself.
"You bastard!" Shitless stomped on the insect several more times, his movements frenzied and desperate. Tears streamed down his face, hot and bitter.
What evil had he committed to deserve this? He is a good monk, so why? Why?! The questions were rhetorical, born of pure anguish.
Crying monk seeing his crying son felt nostalgic, memories of better times washing over him. He let him vent out, understanding that his son needed this release of emotion.

Then he looked at Vritra and spoke, his tears momentarily subsiding: "We will start from tomorrow, I need some rest and want to talk with my son for a bit." His tone carried the weight of someone who had much to discuss, much to explain.

"Alright, Shitless will show you to an empty room." Vritra nodded without hesitation, as they all just watched the family drama unfold. None had expected to see this. The universe certainly had a sense of irony.
What a small world it is.

Soon the two crying monks left, both sharing each other's sadness and grief, their forms disappearing down the hallway with the sound of the staff's rings fading into the distance. Divine was nowhere to be seen, having made himself scarce the moment blame was assigned.
Vritra felt pity towards Shitless, that damned divine really loves to bully everyone. There was a pattern to his cruelty, though.

Only a few hours had passed since they arrived in this realm, and the sky was still bright, golden sunlight streaming through the windows with warmth. But since there was nothing more to do and they can't go out, the oppressive walls of the house seemed to close in. So they decided to return to their room and rest for a bit, seeking solace in quiet spaces.

Gunter and ava left first, moving quietly down the corridor. Then Onest also left, feeling that he should provide a shoulder to cry on to his dear friend. He had an obligation, unspoken but understood.
Now Vritra and the seven women were left there, the silence hanging heavy between them. They too were about to head back when Vritra noticed something peculiar and irritating.
That peeping tom bastard was still staring out of his window, trying to look into the house of darkness. His shamelessness knew no bounds, his persistence like that of some obsessed creature.

"Does he have nothing else to do?" Teresa frowned, her irritation mounting. If he wasn't a higher being she would have already tortured him to death without hesitation. How come there are such pathetic higher beings? The question seemed rhetorical.

Vritra too was getting very annoyed, his jaw clenching slightly as he watched the distant figure. But since he can't beat the other guy just yet, the direct approach wasn't viable. So he would pay back in a different way, through trickery and misdirection. He didn't want to trouble Evelyn for such a small matter, but he wasn't powerless either.
"Let's give his mental health a little shock." He smiled as he glanced at his three daughters, a plan already forming in his mind.
Fiona, Maeve and Teresa. The names carried weight, authority.
They listened to his words, their expressions shifting. And finally felt some excitement at being given a purpose, this should give that perverted turd a lesson he wouldn't forget anytime soon.
Far away in the higher being realm, in a place that existed beyond the normal boundaries of space and perception.

Inside a house that was well protected and covered by several layers of formations, ancient and powerful. No one can listen or see anything about the meeting taking place inside. The walls themselves seemed to absorb all sound and sight, creating a bubble of absolute privacy.
A group of ten people sat behind a long table, their postures formal and aligned. In front of them was a board made of skins of gods, a macabre and powerful artifact that radiated an old authority.

All of them wore white masks and white robes, it was impossible to guess any physical characteristic. The uniformity was deliberate, erasing individuality in favor of collective identity. They all appeared almost same, interchangeable and indistinct.
In front of the board was a man, the only thing differentiating him from others were his six arms and two heads. His form was unsettling to look at, a violation of natural law.
Others had taken over normal human like appearances which was the most common in this realm, a choice that allowed them to move through higher being society more freely.

This was the meeting of the Holy Righteous Heresy group, one of the biggest groups among the higher beings. A faction born from discontent and ambition. And they openly opposed the Vespera family, trying to change the government and law, believing that they were better suited to be the rulers of this realm and its countless subjects.

"Fellow Heretics!" the leader who was called Dipper, spoke in a solemn tone, his voice carrying the weight of centuries of planning. "The time to throw over the current regime and bring bliss to our people is close, we have to put in every bit of effort, use whatever we can to eliminate every single one of Vespera!!" His conviction rang through the chamber like a bell.
"For the Righteousness!"
"For the Heretics!"
They all shouted in unison, their voices merging into a single roar of agreement. Their goals unified through years of shared purpose and mutual hatred.

"How many heretics have joined us so far?" Dipper asked, shifting to practical matters. It was a critical time, finally time to follow the plan and slaughter the Vespera family. They had been planning things for centuries, carefully laying the groundwork. Within a few years, if all went according to plan, they will surely replace them and claim the throne.
"So far we have a total of 1,369 heretics!" one of the commanders replied, pride evident in his tone at the growing numbers.

"Not bad, but even with those numbers, it won't be easy. Just defeating those three monsters will be challenging." Dipper nodded slowly, his assessment sobering but realistic. He had respect for his enemies, even as he plotted their destruction.

Thankfully, they didn't need to fight head on directly. Direct confrontation was suicide. They hadn't been scheming for so many years for nothing. There were other ways, subtler and more effective paths to power.
"Have any contact with the inside been made?" he continued to ask, his tone sharpening with interest.

"Yes, the spies inside the family have contacted that person and they have decided to cooperate with us, these are the conditions they put forth." Another commander passed on a report, sliding it across the table with careful deliberation.

Hearing this, dipper grinned under his mask, a gesture invisible but somehow palpable. Would the great fader and Adam ever expect that there is a mole in their own family? Someone so close to them that they share meals and secrets? It would be great when they get backstabbed later, the irony delicious.

He read the conditions carefully, his expression shifting as his eyes moved across the text. And then he snorted, a sharp sound of dismissal. Muttering: "How shameless, why don't you just ask for the entire realm!" The greed displayed was astounding even by higher being standards.

But that person is still useful, so for now they will cooperate and once the war is won, they simply execute the mole for treachery. Double-crossing a double-crosser felt like poetic justice, though none would appreciate the irony.

"Tell them, we agree to everything except giving them that much land, half the army or the treasury." Dipper said with calculated precision. It was just deceiving but they can't be too obvious, had to maintain the illusion of negotiation. Only seeing them reject some things, would the other party believe them and continue to cooperate.
"Any major recent moments?" dipper looked around, scanning the faces hidden behind masks. After giving few instructions he planned to end the meeting and return to his other obligations.

Instantly, two of the commanders raised their hands simultaneously, signaling they had information to share. Only when Dipper nodded, giving them permission to speak, did one started speaking, choosing his words carefully:
"Uh One of the crooked wants to have a talk with you, sir Dipper." The commander's tone carried uncertainty, as if he wasn't sure how the news would be received.
"Oh!" dipper and the others were surprised at this revelation, their collective reaction visible despite the masks.

After all the hatred between two sides is insurmountable and well documented. They are born enemies, unable to see each other eye to eye, philosophically opposed. Even if they are dying, their last wish would be to eliminate the others. It was especially true for the Crooked, a group whose entire existence seemed defined by opposition.
Those people's life goal itself was killing the higher beings and obtain what they believe should be theirs, a complete reversal of the natural order as understood by the ruling class.
"Where did you meet that Crooked? Who was it? Tell me more." Dipper said with interest, his mind already considering the implications.

He hates crooked too but it would greatly accelerate his plan if he can use them as a weapon against Vespera. Then discarding them would be easy, a simple matter of removing the ladder after climbing.
Thanks for reading... adios

chapters.title: Chapter 883 Pitiful Women
paragraphs: Then the commander began to elaborate, his voice taking on a more cautious tone: "She said her name is Evel, I was exploring a realm and she came out of nowhere. It was as if she knew I was going to be there and she was waiting for me." The commander said, doubt and suspicion heavy in his voice.
He almost started a battle with her, hands moving to weapons instinctively. But she didn't want to fight, her demeanor peaceful and non-threatening.
"She was really strange, unlike all the other Crooked I have seen." The commander added, struggling to articulate what made her different. "There was something almost civilized about her approach."

"Hmm... Interesting, and how will you contact her? She will meet you in that realm again?" a plan flashed in his mind, possibilities branching out before him. But he gave up upon hearing the answer, the hope deflating.

"No, she gave me a jade plate. Telling me that if you don't agree, then just break it, but if it doesn't break in one day, you can talk through it." The commander replied, handing over the artifact as if it might bite.
SIGH

Of course she is very cautious, careful beyond what the Crooked usually displayed. It was a pity but that's fine too. Caution often indicated intelligence, and an intelligent enemy could sometimes be negotiated with.

The commander handed over the jade slip, and dipper put it away into his robe with deliberate care. He didn't break it so his intentions became clear to everyone in the room—he was interested in hearing what the Crooked had to say.

"But colluding with a crooked, is it really alright?" a commander objected, his concerns voiced aloud for the group to consider. Although Vespera needs to be replaced, but it shouldn't be at such a cost, should it? They can't sell their own people without losing their integrity.

"No no, it is no collusion with those foul creatures, we are merely going to make them work for us." Dipper quickly spoke, his tone brooking no argument. Not wanting to start infighting within his own ranks, he smoothed over the concerns with diplomatic precision.
After some discussion that went in circles, they all came to a decision, reluctant but unified.
"What about you?" dipper then looked to the 2nd person who raised his hand, shifting focus away from the touchy subject.
"Today, Evelyn went personally for a case, it was related to that retired drunkard captain, she arrested him." Came the answer, delivered with a certain weight.
"I see, is he in the prison now?" dipper asked, showing little interest at first glance.
The story of that captain had already spread far and wide, who didn't know that he holds a grudge against Evelyn and vice versa. Their mutual antagonism was legendary.
"No, she let him go after some interrogation." The commander's words hung in the air, unexpected and strange.

"Hmmm" dipper frowned deeply, his masked face somehow conveying the expression perfectly. For some reason something felt fishy here, his instincts screaming danger. Although Evelyn had taken action against this captain before too, but this time was something different, something almost calculated.
It was the gut feeling of a higher being, and most of the time their gut feelings is directly influenced by fate itself. And when fate whispered, the wise listened.

"It might just be a normal matter, one of you go and talk to him, and find whatever you can." Dipper said, his tone measured. "If you can recruit him, even better but if you can't then never mind." He wasn't going to force the issue, not when there were bigger fish to fry.

They discussed a few more things, running through logistics and timelines, and the meeting was eventually adjourned. The white-robed figures began to file out, disappearing into the shadows from which they came.
One of the commander as ordered, instantly flew towards the house of darkness with renewed purpose. The fate of their plans might rest on what they discovered.

Inside his house, green pickle was looking at the house of darkness with an intensity that bordered on obsessive. The darkness covering the windows had always been impenetrable, frustrating his attempts at observation. But he persisted nonetheless, his eyes straining against the magical barrier.

He hadn't even received any thank you from those women for saving them. Not a word, not a glance. But then Vritra returned. What had he done to earn such ingratitude? The thought rankled him, bitterness mixing with his self-righteousness.

"Sigh It is fine, he was lucky today I will make sure he gets locked up for life. And save all of them, then surely they will be happy." Green pickle patted his chest with conviction. The fantasy played out in his mind, a scenario where he was the hero that everyone had been waiting for.

But just then, the darkness covering the window disappeared, the magical barrier dropping as if by accident. And he was faintly able to see inside for the first time, the room beyond coming into focus.
He peeped inside quickly, his heart beginning to race with anticipation. And just then, a silhouette appeared in his field of vision. After a moment he found out who it was, recognition dawning.
It was the daughter of that scumbag, the redhead Fiona. She stood there with a terrified look on her face, her body trembling visibly. Her hands clutched at the windowsill as if for support.
'What's wrong with her?' green pickle wondered, his concern and curiosity intermingling. Then he quickly connected the dots and came to a conclusion born of his prejudices.

After what happened earlier, that scumbag Vritra must be in a very bad mood. And he will definitely take his anger out on his family, seeking revenge through those closest to him. The logic seemed airtight to green pickle.
'Damnit! That bastard, how dare he hurt my possible future women!' green pickle felt enraged at the violation of his imagined claims. He quickly began to contact the law holders with urgent fingers.
If he really hurts his family, he will call them again and report, and hopefully Evelyn comes again. She had shown herself to be sympathetic to these women before.
Fiona was shaking her hands, as if trying to say something urgent but unable to form words. Then she wrote something on the window with her finger, each motion deliberate and careful.
'What is she saying? Uh Help... me...?!!' green pickle read it, his eyes widening in shock at the words. The fear in those letters seemed palpable.

And then another woman appeared, stepping into his line of sight. It was Diana, who had a similar pitiful look on her face, her snow-white skin almost luminous in the failing light. Both women still looked extremely beautiful, making green pickle dazed for a few moments as his mind struggled to process what he was seeing. But then he came back to his senses, reality reasserting itself.
Both women were asking for his help, they were in danger! The realization crystallized into urgency within him.

'Should I go over to help?' for a moment, seeing the helpless women he felt brave and capable, his fantasies lending him false confidence. But then remembered how he had been beaten like a dog before, thrown in the sewage where the entire waste of the realm gathers. The memory was fresh, humiliating and painful.
He shuddered and felt that it would be better to call law holders instead. His cowardice rationalized as prudence.
Thus, without wasting any more time he began to contact while looking at the two pitiful women at the window. The phone rang, connecting through channels he wasn't sure even existed.
Diana with her long white hair and snow like skin, appeared so flawless and holy. An angel trapped in a mortal's nightmare.

'Fuck!! Why does that scumbag bastard has such beautiful wives!' green pickle was so angry at the injustice of it all. Thankfully the daughters were also extremely beautiful. So he can make them his main wives, and- The fantasy was taking shape in his mind, getting more detailed and obsessive by the second.
His thoughts were interrupted as the call connected and a voice came from the other side: "How can I help you?" The tone was neutral, professionally bored.
"There is-"
"What the f- Why it is you again? And why am I the only one getting your calls? Hello? I can't hear you, try calling someone else." The law holder quickly cut the call, clearly recognizing the voice.
Then the call came again, and he cut again without even listening. This pattern repeated itself, green pickle being rejected over and over.

After several dozen more tries, green pickle tried relentlessly and so the officer had no choice but to pick the call, if only to end the harassment. "What is it now?" the irritated voice came through, dripping with annoyance.
"I want to report a very serious crime!" green pickle said hurriedly, looking at the two pitiful yet extremely gorgeous women framed in the window. This time it was different, this time it was real.

You damn green tard, everything is very serious for you!! I am sure it is again related to that neighbour of yours. You lecherous bastard, as if not everyone already knows you want to take those women for yourself. The officer thought but didn't say, keeping his professional facade. He asked instead: "Elaborate."
"There are two women asking for he-" just when he was speaking, Vritra appeared behind the two women with sudden and terrifying presence.
There was a sinister and ruthless smile on his face as he made eye contact with green pickle across the distance. ❖❖❖
Thanks for reading...

chapters.title: Chapter 884 An Invitation
paragraphs: "There are two women asking for he-" just when green pickle was speaking, he made an eye contact with Vritra. The moment their eyes met, ice ran down green pickle's spine.

While the two women shuddered in panic and fear, trembling visibly in the dim light, the helplessness on their faces was enough to make anyone pity them and want to protect the two. It was almost like seeing trapped prey.
'No, I can't let that scumbag hurt them!' green pickle thought, urgency coursing through his veins.
"Hurry up, there are two women in danger, one his Diana, his wife and other is Fiona, his daughter." Green pickle hurriedly spoke, his words tumbling over each other in his rush.
But his voice again paused as Vritra suddenly did something pickle hadn't expected. Something that shattered his understanding of the situation entirely.
Vritra suddenly clutched Diana's throat with deliberate slowness, pulling her closer and then captured her lips, ignoring her protest. The kiss was passionate, almost possessive in nature.
'T- That bastard! How dare he-' green pickle was seething with rage, his fists clenching until his knuckles turned white. Then he hurriedly spoke, desperation leaking into his tone:
"Just come here-"
"Sigh What exactly is that neighbour doing?" the law holder on the other side asked in exasperation, clearly losing patience with the repeated calls.
"He- He is suddenly kissing his wife!! You have to come and stop him, hurry!" green pickle said, his voice rising in pitch.
The officer: "..."
There was a long, suffocating silence on the line.

"You green turd, what's the problem with him kissing his wife? And before that, why are you even peeking into someone's house, if you keep bothering, I will lock you up." the officer angrily rebuked, his tone cutting and final.
"B- But..."
Green pickle watched helplessly as Vritra mercilessly devoured Diana's lips, kissing her passionately with an intensity that spoke of genuine desire. The sight felt like a knife to his heart.

But since they turned, he couldn't see anything properly, only seeing Diana struggling in his arms as he continued to kiss her, her body slowly going limp. The struggle seemed to fade, replaced by something else that green pickle couldn't quite interpret from this distance.
Only after a few minutes, when Diana seemed to have no strength in her body and was short on breath, did he finally let go. Her body sagged against him, exhausted.
As she softly slumped down, leaning against Vritra's chest, green pickle felt as if someone had stabbed him and twisted his insides. The pain was almost physical.

He liked Diana and other women, and was confident in protecting them, but now he had failed in the most fundamental way. That pure goddess like woman was getting defiled by that scumbag, he cannot accept that. For a moment he wanted to go and beat him up, wanted to charge over and challenge him to single combat.
But couldn't.
His legs wouldn't move, his courage completely evaporated.
Then he looked at Fiona, Vritra's daughter, at least he cannot do any such things to his daughters. Surely there were boundaries, even for a monster like Vritra.
'But I can't let him beat Fiona, that-'
Yet in the next moment, his eyes widened in shock as Vritra suddenly pulled Fiona into his arms with surprising gentleness, who appeared frozen in fear, her body rigid with tension.
Then, Vritra leaned forward with methodical slowness, pressing his lips against Fiona's. The kiss deepened immediately.
"W- W- What?!! Huh? This... But t- that's his daughter- eh?" green pickle's mind exploded at the sight, his worldview shattering in real time.

He stared in bafflement as Vritra kissed Fiona fervently, devouring her soft red lips with unrestrained passion, even their tongues intertwining in a way that left no doubt about the intimacy. The scene was beyond anything his mind could process.

While kissing her, Vritra glanced towards the stupefied and shaken green pickle across the distance. Their eyes locked for just a moment, and in that brief connection, green pickle felt the weight of Vritra's intent crushing down on him. He had turned pale and was vibrating, every muscle in his body trembling with impotent rage and shock.

'I guess that's enough for now.' Vritra thought, a satisfied smile playing at his lips even as he continued the kiss. Chuckling to himself internally, Vritra pulled the two women deeper into the house with possessive arms, as the curtain of darkness once again blocked everything from view, sealing the house away.
The isolation was complete.
"Are you done? I am disconnecting then-" the officer was getting impatient, his tolerance completely exhausted.

"T- That bastard just kissed his d- daughter!" after a while, green pickle muttered, his voice hollow and distant. His soul seemed to have suffered a critical blow on many levels, shattered in ways he wasn't sure could be repaired.
He liked Fiona and the other daughters, and knew at least they were pure but now? Everything he believed about them, about the world, had been turned upside down.
Soon, the house was thrashed as green pickle went mad, his furniture flying in every direction as he vented his rage and frustration at his impotence.
On the other side, Vritra had already returned to his room, feeling a lot better. The weight of frustration that had been building up inside him had finally been released.
"Hahaha His expressions were hilarious, when you kissed me, that is when he lost it." Fiona laughed, lying beside him on the soft bed, her breathing still slightly elevated.

"Next time, I will also participate in it." Vanessa said from across the room, her role was of Vritra's mother so it would be just as shocking and confusing for the watcher. The thought amused her greatly.
They were just chatting and relaxing when there sounded a knock at the door. The sound was firm, authoritative, and not at all frantic.
"Is it the green turd? Or did he call the law holders?" Maeve wondered, her head resting over Vritra's arm, her expression curious rather than worried.
"I will go check it out." Vritra gently pulled his arm away and got up, moving with unhurried grace.
Then he walked out of the room and paused before the main door, finally able to see the other person clearly through a slight gap. The figure was composed, waiting patiently.
'Now, who is this?' this person clearly wasn't a law holder. He looked normal and had a white mask on his face, pristine and formal. The mask was a calling card in itself.
After a moment of assessment, Vritra opened the door and stepped out, closing the door behind him with deliberate quietness. The outside air hit his skin, cool and neutral.
"..." for a moment, both remained silent, sizing each other up. It was a game both understood, reading the other through posture and subtle movements.
"Hello, you are Vritra right? the former captain of law holders." The other man said, his tone friendly and measured, as if approaching an old acquaintance rather than a stranger.
"I am, and who are you?" although Vritra asked this, but a few guesses formed in his mind already. The white mask was distinctive.
There are only a few organizations who would wear mask like this in this realm openly, and white mask was the trademark of...

"I am from Holy Righteous Heretics, the 10th commander." The man introduced himself then continued: "I have heard what happened recently, from the beginning it was never your fault. I am familiar with your story."

"Haa you were wrongfully accused and punished and even when things came to light, the Vespera family didn't even apologize, ruining your life." His words were carefully chosen, designed to probe reactions.
While speaking, the man observed Vritra's subtle reactions with trained precision, watching for tells and weaknesses.
Right after hearing the word Vespera, Vritra's expressions became twisted, full of rage that seemed to burn from within. His hands clenched involuntarily.
"Just get to the point, what are you here for?" he asked, his eyes burning with barely contained fury.

The man nodded internally, satisfied with the reaction. This guy hates that family to the core, the perfect candidate to be their puppet. Directing hate is so much easier than building loyalty from scratch.

"As you know, we also wish to eradicate the Vespera, reform the laws and build this realm anew. Those Vesperas have ruined everything and needs to be removed." The man said, his voice taking on an almost passionate tone.

And it wasn't a secret that the Holy Righteous Heretics wished to replace Vespera. Even fader and others are aware of their motives, their opposition open but ineffectual. But there always exist some opposition, forces that push back against their plans. Yet this group was secretly adamant at removing them, willing to do anything for that goal.
"So you wish to recruit me?" Vritra asked, cutting through the pleasantries.

"Yes, your strength as the former captain is unquestionable, you were close to being promoted to an even higher position. So not many can challenge you, and I am sure you would want to have your revenge." The man spoke calmly, confidently, as if the outcome was already decided.

"Heh I hate Vespera, especially that Evelyn, so you want to use my anger and turn me into a pawn, using and then discarding? I am not interested." Vritra shook his head with a mocking look, his tone deliberately dismissive.
However internally, he was quite surprised at their boldness.
'These people are so open about it, I did hear that higher beings are always surrounded by chaos but this is just on another level. They don't even bother hiding their intentions.'
Thanks for reading...

Or did he call the law holders?" Maeve wondered, her head resting over Vritra's arm, her expression curious rather than worried.
"I will go check it out." Vritra gently pulled his arm away and got up, moving with unhurried grace.
Then he walked out of the room and paused before the main door, finally able to see the other person clearly through a slight gap.
The figure was composed, waiting patiently.
'Now, who is this?' this person clearly wasn't a law holder.
He looked normal and had a white mask on his face, pristine and formal.
The mask was a calling card in itself.
After a moment of assessment, Vritra opened the door and stepped out, closing the door behind him with deliberate quietness.
The outside air hit his skin, cool and neutral.
"..." for a moment, both remained silent, sizing each other up.
It was a game both understood, reading the other through posture and subtle movements.
"Hello, you are Vritra right? the former captain of law holders." The other man said, his tone friendly and measured, as if approaching an old acquaintance rather than a stranger.
"I am, and who are you?" although Vritra asked this, but a few guesses formed in his mind already.
The white mask was distinctive.
There are only a few organizations who would wear mask like this in this realm openly, and white mask was the trademark of...
"I am from Holy Righteous Heretics, the 10th commander." The man introduced himself then continued: "I have heard what happened recently, from the beginning it was never your fault.
I am familiar with your story."

"Haa you were wrongfully accused and punished and even when things came to light, the Vespera family didn't even apologize, ruining your life." His words were carefully chosen, designed to probe reactions.
While speaking, the man observed Vritra's subtle reactions with trained precision, watching for tells and weaknesses.
Right after hearing the word Vespera, Vritra's expressions became twisted, full of rage that seemed to burn from within.
His hands clenched involuntarily.
"Just get to the point, what are you here for?" he asked, his eyes burning with barely contained fury.
The man nodded internally, satisfied with the reaction.
This guy hates that family to the core, the perfect candidate to be their puppet.
Directing hate is so much easier than building loyalty from scratch.
"As you know, we also wish to eradicate the Vespera, reform the laws and build this realm anew.
Those Vesperas have ruined everything and needs to be removed." The man said, his voice taking on an almost passionate tone.
And it wasn't a secret that the Holy Righteous Heretics wished to replace Vespera.
Even fader and others are aware of their motives, their opposition open but ineffectual.
But there always exist some opposition, forces that push back against their plans.
Yet this group was secretly adamant at removing them, willing to do anything for that goal.
"So you wish to recruit me?" Vritra asked, cutting through the pleasantries.
"Yes, your strength as the former captain is unquestionable, you were close to being promoted to an even higher position.
So not many can challenge you, and I am sure you would want to have your revenge." The man spoke calmly, confidently, as if the outcome was already decided.
"Heh I hate Vespera, especially that Evelyn, so you want to use my anger and turn me into a pawn, using and then discarding?
I am not interested." Vritra shook his head with a mocking look, his tone deliberately dismissive.
However internally, he was quite surprised at their boldness.
'These people are so open about it, I did hear that higher beings are always surrounded by chaos but this is just on another level.
They don't even bother hiding their intentions.'
Thanks for reading...

chapters.title: Chapter 885 The Parting...
paragraphs: " No, no, you misunderstood me. We are not like those evil people. By the order of our great leader Dipper, I ask you to take the position of the 11th Commander, becoming a pillar of our organization. Of course, you would gain more than enough benefits." The man spoke earnestly, his tone shifting to something more sincere.

"..." Vritra paused, considering carefully. With his meager strength, mingling with such powerful people was too dangerous. One tiny mistake and his cover would be blown, exposing him to threats he wasn't prepared for.
But!
Even if they planned to sacrifice him later on, they would surely provide benefits until he was fat and ready to be slaughtered. At the very least, he would gain access to resources and knowledge.

The silence remained for a minute, heavy and charged with possibility, until Vritra finally raised his head and spoke, "Benefits aside, I want to be the one to kill Evelyn. Only then will I join." His voice was cold, final, and absolute.
'Bingo!' the man sneered internally behind his mask. This guy's anger still made him a puppet, controllable and predictable. This was just perfect for their purposes.
'But with his strength, if he can survive the war, he will still be a pillar of the new government, so it's not a total loss for him. At minimum, we get a strong warrior out of this.'
His expressions remained hidden under the white mask, carefully neutral, as the man patted Vritra's shoulder with a gesture of camaraderie.

"Good decision. Take this, it will make things easier to communicate. And I will first inform them back at headquarters, then I will personally invite you to a meeting, where we welcome you as our new Commander."
After saying a few more things, exchanging pleasantries and discussing general expectations, the man turned and flew away into the night sky, disappearing into the shadows.
This meeting was successful. He was sure to get some benefits for this recruitment.
Vritra walked back into the house and closed the door carefully behind him, then looked down at the jade slip that the Commander had left. It was a beautiful piece, crafted with care.

It was supposed to be just for communication, but Vritra could tell it was also meant to observe him, track his movements, and possibly even monitor his thoughts. The surveillance was clumsy but effective.
He threw it into his spatial storage without hesitation, then took out another jade slip from a hidden pocket. It had been given to him by Evelyn.
Of course, it didn't have that surveillance feature. Evelyn didn't need this to look at Vritra. She had other methods, more direct and intimate ones.
'Heh, time to snitch.'
Vritra inserted his mana into the jade slip with practiced ease, which instantly connected to Evelyn, establishing a channel across the vast distance.
"My love, are you missing me already? Should I come meet you?" Her overly enthusiastic and obsessive voice came from the other side, tinged with possessiveness.
Vritra rolled his eyes at the greeting, then spoke, "I just got a special guest..."
He relayed the information methodically, leaving nothing out.
"And thus, I joined them." He ended the explanation, but for now, there was no real inside information.
Evelyn and the Vespera Family were well aware of that group's motives.
"You shouldn't join them. It would be too dangerous." Evelyn frowned on the other side. Rather than being pleased by the information, she prioritized his safety.
"It will be fine. I will at least survive even if they do find anything suspicious." Vritra reassured her.
Evelyn tried a bit more but knew it was impossible to change his decision, so she gave up.
Instead, she decided to create a treasure for him that could protect him.
Then the call disconnected. Vritra returned to his room, and all his wives had heard about the entire conversation.
Yet, they were more surprised by how Vritra talked to Evelyn. Weren't they enemies before?
At least, he didn't seem to like her all that much.
"Looks like we have nothing to do for today, so how about I help you all with some exercise?" Vritra asked, and without giving any time to his wives, a battle started in the room.
1st round, 2nd, then 3rd, and it kept on going hour after hour.
The exercise was so intense that after a few hours, one by one, all the wives were exhausted.
But being the diligent husband, Vritra didn't allow them to slack off, and it continued on until very late into the night.
Only after 2 did they finally fall asleep.
Everyone in the House of Darkness was woken up by the chanting of some Buddhist prayers, along with the wailing from the surrounding Higher Beings.
Vritra and the rest weren't affected like the others, but it was like someone snoring close to them, very unpleasant.
So, they woke up early and got ready.
By 6 in the morning, everyone had gathered in the hall.
Shitless, after the previous day's revelation and sadness, looked fine now.
Beside him stood the Crying Monk with his towering body, holding the metallic staff and giving off a powerful vibe.

"Benefactors, are you all ready to start your training? Let me warn you, though. I can just bring you to your fortune. The rest will be in your own hands, and the most I can do is preserve your lives." The Crying Monk spoke seriously.
Vritra didn't speak immediately. Instead, he looked at everyone in his family.
"We are ready."
One by one, they all nodded, determination burning in their eyes.
"My son, your opportunity lies back at home. Your challenges will be just as hard, though, if not more." The Crying Monk patted Shitless's head.
"Yes, father." Shitless nodded.
There was a brief pause, then the Crying Monk looked at everyone and added, "After this, you all won't be able to meet each other for some time."
"..." The group looked at each other. Always staying together, it felt strange to suddenly part.
Yet, this was unavoidable.
"Don't worry. After the initial difficult part passes, you will be able to meet." At this moment, Divine appeared and spoke, not looking at his pet.
This made them relax.
Vritra suddenly remembered something. His hand extended, and in the next second, the entire house was filled with blinding light.
A small sun appeared floating over his palm. It was the 4th-ranked Mythic Halo, the Sun.
It had been kindly given to them as a gift from the gods after the court case, and he had forgotten about it.
He could use it, but it actually didn't suit him that much. Instead, his target was the 2nd-ranked Mythic Halo, the Demonic Veyll.
Among all his wives, Yasmine was the one who was most suitable for this Mythic Halo.
And she didn't possess any powerful weapon either, unlike Vanessa, Yennefer, Fiona, Maeve, or Diana.
Now only Teresa would be left, who would need some strong weapon.
Vanessa had that cloth, Yennefer had the Time Staff, Fiona had the Undying Mythic Halo, Maeve had the Blade of Darkness, and Diana had that blue knife and the Tomb of Gods.
"Wifey, this is for you."
The Sun floated toward Yasmine, gently landing over her hand.
Although it possessed such a high temperature, none of them felt anything.
"Thank you, hubby." Yasmine smiled. After looking at it, she put it away.
If he gave it to her, it naturally suited her more. Thankfully, there was no jealousy over such things in the family.
Shitless would get something from the Crying Monk, so Onest would be left too.
But there was no hurry.
"That's a good thing. Anyway, after you are done with your goodbyes, follow after me."
After saying so, the Crying Monk gently tapped the metallic staff against the ground, and ten portals opened before them.
With Shitless, who waved his hand with two streaks of tears falling down his cheek, he walked into one of them.
"Stay safe. I will do my best to grow stronger." Onest smiled faintly, looking at them before walking into another portal.
Divine had already left.
Instantly, all the women looked at each other sadly and then at Vritra.
They were going to miss everyone, and especially miss Vritra. That was a long period of time.
"Honey, don't do anything reckless and hurt yourself. I will miss you a lot." Vanessa hugged Vritra tightly before pressing her lips against his.
The kiss wasn't like usual. Their lips remained pressed together for a bit before finally parting.
Since it was only a short goodbye, Vanessa didn't want it to turn any sadder, so after a few minutes, she left.
Then the other wives all followed, giving parting hugs and kisses to Vritra.
Yennefer was the 2nd to hug and kiss him, even biting his lip so she could remember his taste even amidst the tough training.
Then came Fiona. The redhead left a mark on Vritra's neck, making him laugh at her intense actions.
Patting her head, he whispered sweet nothings into her ear, and finally, she reluctantly left.
Then it was Diana. The goddess was very sad to part. They had stayed together for so long.
It reminded her of that time when Vritra died after the war, filling her with sadness.
Soon, she too entered, then Teresa kissed Vritra just as he was waving toward the goddess.
The goth girl hugged him tightly for a while, filling her body and clothes with his scent and warmth before parting.
Vritra turned and patted the pouting foxie, her tail hanging low, making her look cute and pitiful.
"Don't be sad. We will be together very soon anyway." He said, capturing her lips and making her feel a little better.
Finally, only Yasmine was left there. Vritra walked toward her and pulled her into his arms.
"Wifey, take care of yourself and our baby. I will come to meet you as soon as possible."
"Mhmm..."
Thanks for reading... adios

chapters.title: Chapter 886 The Training Arc
paragraphs: Passing through the portal, Onest found himself standing in an endless field, with tiny grass growing sparsely across the barren landscape.
It almost appeared like an enormous football stadium, devoid of spectators and life.
"This will be your training area for the next 400 months." Suddenly a voice sounded from behind Onest, echoing across the empty expanse.
Upon turning, he found that it was the crying monk, hadn't he gone with Shitless? His sudden appearance was jarring.
But that wasn't important, frowning he asked: "400? The time here flows differently from the outside?" His mind was already racing with the implications.

"Exactly" crying monk nodded, then started explaining: "Your status will soon rise to level 10 demi god, but those gods are very strong, so I will do my best to increase your strength as much as possible."
There was a heaviness to his words, an understanding of the burden ahead.

"Uh Okay, so what are we going to do? Do we spar? What about that God's mana?" Onest questioned, taking a step back, crying monk now looked far more serious than before, his demeanor shifting entirely.
"Right, the god's mana is the key. It holds a high value, not just energy, but experience, skills and more, making it merge with you will be tough but doable."
Crying monk stared at Onest intently, as if he can see through all his secrets and skills, penetrating layers of his being.
In the next moment, crying monk gently tapped the ground with the staff, illuminating the whole place with radiant light. His body disappeared in a shimmer.

Then the place was filled with dust and loud roars, startling Onest, who looked around frantically and soon saw a lineup of infinite bulls, each twice as big as normal bulls, their forms imposing and terrifying.
It was like an army, standing in formation, line after line, a sea of horns and muscle. Crying monk was seated on the first one, observing from his elevated position.
"What is this?" Onest froze, his breath catching in his throat. The energies emanating from those bulls was so high, as if they were all level 10 demi gods, far beyond his current comprehension.
How can this be?

"This is the best way to hone yourself, try to dodge. Whether you get hit or not, the god's mana will boil and rebuild you, do you best!" Crying monk shouted as all the bulls roared in unison, a deafening sound that shook the very ground.
They thumped the earth before surging forward, engulfing everything in sight with relentless momentum.

Onest's heart skipped a beat, at his fullest speed he started running in the opposite direction, desperation driving his movements. But it was useless. He couldn't match the speed of those bulls, they were closing in rapidly.
In the next moment, he felt the large and sharp horns of the bulls hit his back with crushing force, throwing him into the sky.
The attack didn't injure Onest much but there was still some pain, sharp and immediate.
He did his best to dodge, weaving between attacks desperately, but soon he was engulfed by the bulls, sometimes getting stomped, bit and what not. His body took blow after blow.

At the same time, the god's mana in his body started to rage over, violently climbing all over his body like wildfire, burning and healing simultaneously. Just like that, Onest's 400 months long torture began in earnest.
Another clone of the crying monk appeared in a land that was filled with countless colours, a dance of aurora lighting up the realm. The light seemed alive, shifting and pulsing with ancient power.
There was no land, air, or even space, just a mix of infinite elements, all of it could be found in the light that seemed to be devouring everything around it, hungry and consuming.
This was the training area for Yennefer, mainly because of her very special physique, which can encompass all elements with unique harmony.
Although not as special as the titans, this physique was also extremely unique and powerful, ranked high among the rarest of abilities. While also very difficult to master and control.
Almost all those who possessed this physique in the history were assimilated into the very world, disappearing without a trace and died, lost to the very power they tried to wield.

Yennefer had started to experiencing the beginning of that phenomenon not long ago, suddenly her body transforming into a random element without warning. So, it was both a treasure and a time bomb ticking within her very essence.
And that was crying monk's goal for Yennefer, using the god's mana to unlock full potential of her body and let her have complete control over it, to master what had destroyed others before her.
The gods wouldn't be able to do anything if she really managed to do that. This wouldn't be easy and was far more dangerous than what Onest was going through, the stakes far higher.
Her body, mind and soul all merged into the light with infinite colours and elements, violent waves of energy expanding outward in destructive arcs.
The time limit for her was even more dramatic than Onest, demanding absolute focus and will, and thus the challenge dancing over life and death began without mercy.
In a completely different realm, Fiona stood against an infinite number of beings whose body was burning with red flames, their forms wreathed in crimson fire.
Each of those opponents were incredibly powerful that she cannot defeat them individually, overwhelming in their sheer numbers and strength.
Plus they were also able to use the undying mythic halo, making them nigh impossible to kill permanently.
Her challenge was to break them all and the time would stretch until she does it, no mercy or shortcuts offered.
Of course her life would always be protected by the training structure, but the challenge was still terrifyingly difficult and dangerous to face.
As she clashed with the opponents repeatedly, the god's mana surged all over her body in violent spirals.
The undying mythic halo burst out with every exchange of attacks, creating brilliant displays of power.
But for every attack she delivered, Fiona was attacked at immense speed over 100 times, the overwhelming assault forcing her to push beyond her limits.
Crying monk stood far away and observed her battle style intently, this will improve her in a lot of fields and aspects.
Fiona thus entangled in a brutal battle without end.
Contrary to them, vanessa was sitting on a platform, the place completely peaceful and serene, a stark contrast to the chaos elsewhere.
The god's mana like an enormous planet floating above her head, glowing with soft luminescence.
She appeared extremely tiny before it, dwarfed by its magnitude. The platform cracked and reformed under the pressure of the mana, struggling to maintain integrity.

As a succubus, her battle style was completely different from the others, her approach unique. She doesn't need to engage in a bloody battle like Fiona or others. She needed to hone things like her soul, mental fortitude and more, deeper aspects of her being.
A cloth floated around her body, extracting mana as it continued to merge with her body, rapidly increasing her strength at a steady pace.

Although not as painful as the others, but it made her feel so full as if about to explode before she quickly channelled and absorbed it all in controlled waves. Before the cloth extracted more energy relentlessly.

Her defences were quickly rising with each absorption, even her charms were rising at a visible rate before her eyes. Her beauty becoming more and more enchanting and radiant, while her mana reserves already looking like a surging sea, flooding over every moment without rest.
With her own challenges, vanessa continued on her own path forward.
Similarly to Fiona, Yasmine was also experiencing a great battle, her draconic nature demanding constant combat.
She still needed to absorb and assimilate the Sun mythic halo with its burning power.
Thus similarly and also differently to vanessa, two large orbs of energy were revolving above her head, orbiting like celestial bodies.

As the fight continued relentlessly, her body continued to grow stronger, absorbing both energies in tandem. She then turned into her draconic form, scales shimmering, going completely wild and absorbing the energies even faster with primal hunger.

The crying monk, being considerate towards her had made it such that time will move in a way that even if many many years pass here, time for Yasmine personally would move extremely slowly, stretched and gentle.
After all she is pregnant, so even if she stay years here, it would barely be a month or two at most for her child.
And thus, without worrying about her unborn child Yasmine also started training with full commitment.

Maeve, being a demonic fox and controller of darkness was growing in a different direction from others, her path unique. Her speciality lay in hidden attacks and quickly killing enemies with precision strikes. Thus the main focus of her training was not just increasing her defences or raw power.
Instead it was mainly increasing her agility, reaction speed, merging and controlling the darkness better and more intimately.
She was present in a dark space with nothing around, yet enemies darker than darkness present everywhere surrounding her.
Each one she defeated would bring her countless insights, and new skills to master.
Her path was of an overpowered assassin or rather far more than that, something transcendent.

Teresa's path was different from all others distinctly, her main strength lay in her brain and intellect. So the crying monk had brought her into an inventory where she can find almost any object that could be found in the countless galaxies, precious and worthless alike.

All the great and small inventions from different places, opening new horizons for her mind to explore. While the mana would slowly merge, it would increase her physical capabilities to support her fighting style, especially her mana pool and reserves.
While she could focus on creating treasures on power levels of the higher beings, though that would need more time and resources. So for now on the level of the gods, which was challenge enough.

Diana was currently submerged in the tomb of the gods, surrounded by ancient power. The god's mana had already merged with her body easily, it was too compatible with her and needed only a few days, unlike the others who struggled.
Her status rose quickly, her strength already far higher than others at this moment in the training grounds.
But her hurdle now was to defeat all the gods in the tomb of gods, completely absorb their divine abilities, their status, their profound natures and more.
Although the absorption of god's mana was too easy for her naturally, her current challenge was just as tough and demanding.
And just like that, she completely focussed on her tasks ahead.

sentences.text: Passing through the portal, Onest found himself standing in an endless field, with tiny grass growing sparsely across the barren landscape.
It almost appeared like an enormous football stadium, devoid of spectators and life.
"This will be your training area for the next 400 months." Suddenly a voice sounded from behind Onest, echoing across the empty expanse.
Upon turning, he found that it was the crying monk, hadn't he gone with Shitless?
His sudden appearance was jarring.
But that wasn't important, frowning he asked: "400?
The time here flows differently from the outside?" His mind was already racing with the implications.

"Exactly" crying monk nodded, then started explaining: "Your status will soon rise to level 10 demi god, but those gods are very strong, so I will do my best to increase your strength as much as possible."
There was a heaviness to his words, an understanding of the burden ahead.
"Uh Okay, so what are we going to do?
Do we spar?
What about that God's mana?" Onest questioned, taking a step back, crying monk now looked far more serious than before, his demeanor shifting entirely.
"Right, the god's mana is the key.
It holds a high value, not just energy, but experience, skills and more, making it merge with you will be tough but doable."
Crying monk stared at Onest intently, as if he can see through all his secrets and skills, penetrating layers of his being.
In the next moment, crying monk gently tapped the ground with the staff, illuminating the whole place with radiant light.
His body disappeared in a shimmer.

Then the place was filled with dust and loud roars, startling Onest, who looked around frantically and soon saw a lineup of infinite bulls, each twice as big as normal bulls, their forms imposing and terrifying.
It was like an army, standing in formation, line after line, a sea of horns and muscle.
Crying monk was seated on the first one, observing from his elevated position.
"What is this?" Onest froze, his breath catching in his throat.
The energies emanating from those bulls was so high, as if they were all level 10 demi gods, far beyond his current comprehension.
How can this be?
"This is the best way to hone yourself, try to dodge.
Whether you get hit or not, the god's mana will boil and rebuild you, do you best!" Crying monk shouted as all the bulls roared in unison, a deafening sound that shook the very ground.
They thumped the earth before surging forward, engulfing everything in sight with relentless momentum.
Onest's heart skipped a beat, at his fullest speed he started running in the opposite direction, desperation driving his movements.
But it was useless.
He couldn't match the speed of those bulls, they were closing in rapidly.
In the next moment, he felt the large and sharp horns of the bulls hit his back with crushing force, throwing him into the sky.
The attack didn't injure Onest much but there was still some pain, sharp and immediate.
He did his best to dodge, weaving between attacks desperately, but soon he was engulfed by the bulls, sometimes getting stomped, bit and what not.
His body took blow after blow.
At the same time, the god's mana in his body started to rage over, violently climbing all over his body like wildfire, burning and healing simultaneously.
Just like that, Onest's 400 months long torture began in earnest.
Another clone of the crying monk appeared in a land that was filled with countless colours, a dance of aurora lighting up the realm.
The light seemed alive, shifting and pulsing with ancient power.
There was no land, air, or even space, just a mix of infinite elements, all of it could be found in the light that seemed to be devouring everything around it, hungry and consuming.
This was the training area for Yennefer, mainly because of her very special physique, which can encompass all elements with unique harmony.
Although not as special as the titans, this physique was also extremely unique and powerful, ranked high among the rarest of abilities.
While also very difficult to master and control.
Almost all those who possessed this physique in the history were assimilated into the very world, disappearing without a trace and died, lost to the very power they tried to wield.
Yennefer had started to experiencing the beginning of that phenomenon not long ago, suddenly her body transforming into a random element without warning.
So, it was both a treasure and a time bomb ticking within her very essence.
And that was crying monk's goal for Yennefer, using the god's mana to unlock full potential of her body and let her have complete control over it, to master what had destroyed others before her.
The gods wouldn't be able to do anything if she really managed to do that.
This wouldn't be easy and was far more dangerous than what Onest was going through, the stakes far higher.
Her body, mind and soul all merged into the light with infinite colours and elements, violent waves of energy expanding outward in destructive arcs.
The time limit for her was even more dramatic than Onest, demanding absolute focus and will, and thus the challenge dancing over life and death began without mercy.
In a completely different realm, Fiona stood against an infinite number of beings whose body was burning with red flames, their forms wreathed in crimson fire.
Each of those opponents were incredibly powerful that she cannot defeat them individually, overwhelming in their sheer numbers and strength.
Plus they were also able to use the undying mythic halo, making them nigh impossible to kill permanently.
Her challenge was to break them all and the time would stretch until she does it, no mercy or shortcuts offered.
Of course her life would always be protected by the training structure, but the challenge was still terrifyingly difficult and dangerous to face.
As she clashed with the opponents repeatedly, the god's mana surged all over her body in violent spirals.
The undying mythic halo burst out with every exchange of attacks, creating brilliant displays of power.
But for every attack she delivered, Fiona was attacked at immense speed over 100 times, the overwhelming assault forcing her to push beyond her limits.
Crying monk stood far away and observed her battle style intently, this will improve her in a lot of fields and aspects.
Fiona thus entangled in a brutal battle without end.
Contrary to them, vanessa was sitting on a platform, the place completely peaceful and serene, a stark contrast to the chaos elsewhere.
The god's mana like an enormous planet floating above her head, glowing with soft luminescence.
She appeared extremely tiny before it, dwarfed by its magnitude.
The platform cracked and reformed under the pressure of the mana, struggling to maintain integrity.
As a succubus, her battle style was completely different from the others, her approach unique.
She doesn't need to engage in a bloody battle like Fiona or others.
She needed to hone things like her soul, mental fortitude and more, deeper aspects of her being.
A cloth floated around her body, extracting mana as it continued to merge with her body, rapidly increasing her strength at a steady pace.
Although not as painful as the others, but it made her feel so full as if about to explode before she quickly channelled and absorbed it all in controlled waves.
Before the cloth extracted more energy relentlessly.
Her defences were quickly rising with each absorption, even her charms were rising at a visible rate before her eyes.
Her beauty becoming more and more enchanting and radiant, while her mana reserves already looking like a surging sea, flooding over every moment without rest.
With her own challenges, vanessa continued on her own path forward.
Similarly to Fiona, Yasmine was also experiencing a great battle, her draconic nature demanding constant combat.
She still needed to absorb and assimilate the Sun mythic halo with its burning power.
Thus similarly and also differently to vanessa, two large orbs of energy were revolving above her head, orbiting like celestial bodies.
As the fight continued relentlessly, her body continued to grow stronger, absorbing both energies in tandem.
She then turned into her draconic form, scales shimmering, going completely wild and absorbing the energies even faster with primal hunger.

The crying monk, being considerate towards her had made it such that time will move in a way that even if many many years pass here, time for Yasmine personally would move extremely slowly, stretched and gentle.
After all she is pregnant, so even if she stay years here, it would barely be a month or two at most for her child.
And thus, without worrying about her unborn child Yasmine also started training with full commitment.
Maeve, being a demonic fox and controller of darkness was growing in a different direction from others, her path unique.
Her speciality lay in hidden attacks and quickly killing enemies with precision strikes.
Thus the main focus of her training was not just increasing her defences or raw power.
Instead it was mainly increasing her agility, reaction speed, merging and controlling the darkness better and more intimately.
She was present in a dark space with nothing around, yet enemies darker than darkness present everywhere surrounding her.
Each one she defeated would bring her countless insights, and new skills to master.
Her path was of an overpowered assassin or rather far more than that, something transcendent.
Teresa's path was different from all others distinctly, her main strength lay in her brain and intellect.
So the crying monk had brought her into an inventory where she can find almost any object that could be found in the countless galaxies, precious and worthless alike.
All the great and small inventions from different places, opening new horizons for her mind to explore.
While the mana would slowly merge, it would increase her physical capabilities to support her fighting style, especially her mana pool and reserves.
While she could focus on creating treasures on power levels of the higher beings, though that would need more time and resources.
So for now on the level of the gods, which was challenge enough.
Diana was currently submerged in the tomb of the gods, surrounded by ancient power.

chapters.title: Chapter 887 The Titan's Fragments
paragraphs: Vritra stood before a spatial crack, with absolutely nothing around him stretching endlessly.
But a deadly suction force was constantly gushing out of the broken space, enough to pull gods or even higher beings toward oblivion.
The force was relentless, hungry, a vacuum that demanded to consume.
Crying monk stood not too far away, a barrier protecting them both from the devastating pull. His form remained steady, unaffected by the chaos.
"This place is a prison or also called a death zone, a place where the higher beings and others pushed one of the most dangerous species."
The crying monk spoke, looking at the realm with a mixture of reverence and caution. His voice carried the weight of ancient history.
The crack seemed to pull all the surrounding galaxies, planets, as if trying to devour them whole, an endless maw of destruction.
"...The Titans?" Vritra asked, wondering what his training would include, a chill running down his spine.
"You have a choice, two paths ahead of you.
The difficulty, time and your resulting strength will depend on your choice." The monk's tone was serious, brooking no levity.
Hearing this, Vritra nodded slowly, waiting for the crying monk to continue, his mind already calculating possibilities.

"The first path will be a bit easy, it will bring your to godhood and without a doubt your strength will be enough to win the future war against the gods, then we won't enter this realm and move to a different training ground." He paused, letting the words settle.
"I see, and the second choice is?" Vritra's voice remained calm despite his racing thoughts.
"Directly aiming for the higher being realm!" crying monk's voice resounded powerfully, carrying a heavy weight that seemed to shake the very air around them.

Vritra didn't instantly make a choice, before asking carefully: "And what are the disadvantages of choosing this 2nd option aside from its difficulty?" He needed to understand the full scope before committing.

"There are many, the pain you will feel at many levels might be too much for your mind to endure, the time it will take will be so long you might start to forget your own existence, you might just end up dead and some more things."
Crying monk counted over his fingers methodically, each point more grim than the last.
Vritra: "..."
After a long silence he asked, his tone measured: "What are the chances of success?" He needed numbers, concrete probabilities.
"Hmm Originally... zero." The crying monk said matter of factly, his expression grave.
"And now with you being here?" Vritra pressed, seeking some glimmer of hope.
"It's 20-80." Crying monk replied, after calculating something carefully in his mind.
"20 that I die and 80 that I succeed? Not bad." Vritra nodded, as expected the crying monk is quite capable. His lips twitched slightly upward.
"No no, it's the opposite. 80 you die, 20 you might succeed, it will depend mainly on your efforts." Came the reply, delivered without mercy or sugar-coating.
Vritra once again fell silent, his mind absorbing the weight of those odds. Even in 20, there is a might? He cursed divine and the crying monk a few times in his mind bitterly before asking:
"Is there really even a chance of success? If the chances of death is so high, why would you bring me here?" His frustration was evident but controlled.
"Although this step will bring me directly to higher beings level, but there are two many problems, don't you have any other method?" He paused, collecting his thoughts.

"Even though he would very much like to get stronger quickly, but that doesn't mean he would gamble with his life when failure is almost guaranteed. He can take things slow and grow to that level eventually."
"There are other ways but they will take too long and has even lower chances of success." The crying monk began, then raised a hand.
"But!"
He paused dramatically, making Vritra roll his eyes internally. This bald monk really seemed to enjoy such theatrical moments.
The monk continued: "I do have a way to increase the chances greatly, but how much it will increase will depend on your hard work, diligence and obsession, also your fate.
The success might even increase to over 90 or be reduced to 0."
"I see." Vritra still didn't reply immediately but asked further, his expression thoughtful. "How long will this take?"
"For you it will be a long long time, hundreds of thousands of years even, maybe more, I'm not sure." Crying monk replied uncertainly, scratching his chin.
"But in the outside world, it will be around 5 to 6 months." He paused, reconsidering. "Clearly, it might even take longer."
"Then that would be impossible, the game will be held in around four months, not to mention I still to do some things in the higher beings realm." Vritra frowned deeply, seeing a critical obstacle.
He had joined the Holy Righteous Heretics, so to get more information and benefits he would need to be present there actively.
"I have already thought of a solution for that, so its not a problem." Crying monk said, shrugging as if it were a minor detail.
"Not to mention, I have to be there with Yasmine." Vritra added, another layer of constraint.
Hearing this, the crying monk fell into deep thoughts, his expression shifting as possibilities arranged themselves. After a while he spoke:
"With a little management of time, that could be handled as well, so not much time would pass for her personally."
Vritra thought for a bit, his mind running through the scenarios.
There didn't seem to be any more problems standing in the way, and crying monk definitely wanted him to choose this option. The desire was palpable.
"Okay then I will go with this." He finally spoke, commitment settling over him like a cloak.
Nodding, crying monk spoke as if he had already expected this outcome: "Then let's get you a bit geared up." His tone shifted to something more practical.
After speaking, the crying monk tapped his staff gently against the ground. It suddenly underwent a dramatic transformation before Vritra's eyes.
Nodding, crying monk spoke as if he had already expected this outcome: "Then let's get you a bit geared up." His tone shifted to something more practical.
After speaking, the crying monk tapped his staff gently against the ground. It suddenly underwent a dramatic transformation before Vritra's eyes.

It became a black staff as if made from a spatial fragment itself, with countless tiny rings around the top shimmering with power. Near the base, it became perfectly round and smooth, gleaming with dark luminescence.
"Here, this will help you traverse in that endless space, navigating what should be unnavigable." The monk handed it over carefully.
"It can also be charged up with the more titan's fragments you kill or collect which can then be used for defence or offence as needed."
"And! These rings you see is like a life token, each time you die, one ring will break and you will be restored."
The monk pointed to the gleaming rings encircling the staff. "Still you will have to be very careful, this place is too dangerous beyond measure."
Vritra nodded, taking the staff and feeling its weight settle in his hands. This staff was certainly a top grade treasure even among the higher beings, a weapon of legend.
And if he was getting so many extra lives embedded within it, the challenge is going to be extremely difficult, hell or maybe impossible level.
'But if I can do it, then I won't have to hide among the higher beings anymore.' He thought, a spark of determination igniting within.
"What exactly will I have to do?" Vritra questioned carefully, as crying monk passed on the space and began to explain:
"The titans were thrown into that rift since their very existence was too dangerous and no one truly had any proper way to deal with them effectively."
The monk's voice took on a historical quality. "And in this place, the titans all killed one another and devoured them over eons. But!"
The crying monk again paused dramatically, making Vritra roll his eyes visibly this time. This bald monk really seemed to enjoy pausing like that in the conversations, building tension.
"But what?" Vritra asked impatiently, waiting for the revelation.
"But there appeared a variable, the divine! He allowed the last and the strongest titan to escape, in a way with your help unknowingly."

The monk's expression grew complex. "But he also stopped that final titan from completely devouring all the titans, so although they are all dead, the fragments of the titans has scattered across that space like seeds."
"And you have to collect all those fragments and devour them, by the end you will be at a level of powerful higher beings." The monk gestured expansively toward the rift.
"As difficult as it is, the reward will be great beyond measure."
Vritra listened carefully, absorbing every word. From what he heard before, collecting these fragments won't be easy nor the same for all the fragments.
Crying monk had even mentioned killing some fragments directly, but now he has a concrete goal to pursue.
Whatever it is, he will do his best to succeed.
"Now finally, what do you plan about the god's war and me staying in the higher being realm? And what about the god's mana?" he asked, clearing his mind of distractions.
These were the practical concerns.

"That is easy, I will just create a puppet for you, an exact copy to take your place." The crying monk said casually. "As for that God's mana, it will be of a great help to you once you start consuming the fragments."
Right after speaking, the crying monk made a grabbing motion toward Vritra's arm. Then a drop of Vritra's blood was extracted along with a tiny piece of his skin, glowing softly as it left his body.
Thanks for reading...
